problem: The ns-gm CLI provides runtime inspection capabilities for NetSuite environments (execute SuiteScript code, retrieve script execution logs). For the 'Monitoring with Auto Solve' feature, ns-gm is the tool through which the monitoring agent will probe NetSuite production environments to check monitoring plan conditions (log patterns, record states, governance usage).

files.why: NetSuite RESTlet that handles 'run' (execute SuiteScript) and 'getscriptexecutionlogs' (retrieve logs) actions. The monitoring agent will use both actions. The RESTlet provides governance tracking (initial/remaining/used) and all major NS modules (search, query, record, runtime, log, etc.).
Local Express proxy with /run, /logs, /health endpoints. Routes requests to the NetSuite RESTlet via OAuth 2.0 authentication. The monitoring agent calls these endpoints.
OAuth 2.0 M2M token management with JWT client assertion. Handles token caching and refresh. Monitoring requires authenticated access to NetSuite.
CLI logs command with filtering (date range, log type, script ID, pagination). The monitoring agent will query logs to check for expected positive/negative patterns.
CLI run command for executing SuiteScript. The monitoring agent can run custom SuiteScript to check record states, search for specific conditions, or verify business logic.
Environment detection (SANDBOX vs PRODUCTION). Monitoring should verify it is checking the production environment, not sandbox.
Credential storage and retrieval. Multi-profile support allows pointing to different NS environments. The server manages NS-GM credentials via NsGmCredential model.
Agent guidance document describing core architecture, credential model, and command surface.
Dependencies: axios, commander, express, jose, prompts. Scripts: start (node src/cli.js). No build/lint/test scripts.

facts: ns-gm is a CLI + local Express proxy that routes requests to a NetSuite RESTlet via OAuth 2.0 M2M authentication.
Two main actions: 'run' (execute arbitrary SuiteScript with module injection) and 'getscriptexecutionlogs' (retrieve NS script execution logs with filtering).

Available NS modules for code execution: log, search, record, runtime, format, query, transaction, file, https, http, email, error, url, encode, crypto, currency, render, xml, config, task, redirect, cache, certificateControl, workflow.
Log retrieval supports filtering by: date range (dateFrom/dateTo), log type (DEBUG, AUDIT, ERROR, EMERGENCY), script ID, pagination (pageIndex/pageSize).
Governance tracking: every response includes initial, remaining, and used governance units.
Multi-profile credential storage at ~/.ns-gm/credentials.json. Profiles are alias-based and can point to different NS environments (SANDBOX/PRODUCTION).

The helix-global-server manages NS-GM credentials per-organization via NsGmCredential model with encrypted private keys. The server can prepare NS-GM credentials for sandbox execution (prepareNsGmCredential in ns-gm-credentials.ts).
No existing monitoring, scheduling, or agent infrastructure in ns-gm. It is a stateless CLI tool.
No build/lint/test/typecheck scripts defined in package.json. Plain JavaScript (not TypeScript).
Proxy inactivity timeout: 15 minutes (config.json). Server listens on port 9292.
